caseno: Death Reference No.12 of 1994 with Criminal Appeal No.1514 of 1994 and Jail Appeal No. 1177 of 1994.
lawyer:
Syed Abu Kowser, Assistant Attorney-General --- For the State. 
Shaukat Ali Khan with Fazlul Haque Khan Farid, Md Tamizuddin and Mustafa Zaman Islam, Advocates --- For the Condemned-Prisoner and Accused-Appellants.
parties:
State ------ Appellant
Vs.
Ali Hossain and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that PW 2 Sanwar Hossain lodged the FIR with Kaliakoir Police Station, Gazipur on 9-6-1992 alleging, inter alia, that he was a son of the victim A. Sattar by his first wife. A Sattar was a resident of village Bhangra Jorebari, PS Bashail, District-Tangail. After liberation of Bangladesh Abdus Sattar took second wife accused appellant Jamila Khatun and due to discord and disagreement on this account with his first wife went to and started residing with the father of his second wife in 1993 at village Joynatali, PS Sreepur in the District of Gazipur. After having lived there for 4 years A. Sattar left the house of his father-in-law and started residing in the village named Ramchandrapur with his second wife Jamila Khatun within PS Kaliakoir by constructing a but there. At about 12 AM on 8-6-92 the informant (PW 2) being informed by PW 7 Polu Mia that his father A Sattar was murdered in his house left for Ramchandrapur along with his uncle PW 9 Momrej Ali, mother Jamena and cousin brother Delwar Hosaain and Kuddus and found A Sattar dead in his house with various injuries on his head, forehead and chest. He learned from the local people that during the night of occurrence his step mother accused appellant Jamila Khatun was with his father in the same hut. His step-mother had quarrel with his father for quite some time before the occurrence and she even threatened to leave his father. He therefore suspected that his step-mother accused appellant Jamila was actively involved in the murder of his father A Sattar. 

 7. PW 1 Dr Md Ali Haider Khan conducted the post-mortem examination of the dead body of A Sattar and found several incised wounds on the head, forehead, neck and other parts of the dead body of A Sattar and opined that all these injuries were inflicted by heavy sharp cutting weapon which were ante-mortem and homicidal in nature and the death was caused due to serious hemorrhage from the aforesaid injuries. 

 8. PW 2 Sanwar Hossain is the informant and a son of the victim Abdus Sattar. This witness deposed along the line of the allegations contained in the FIR. He stated that after being informed of the death of father Abdus Sattar he along with his other relations went to village Ramchandrapur and found his father dead in the place of occurrence house with serious bleeding injuries on his chest, neck and forehead. 

 9. PW 3 Md Younus Talukder was the officer-in-charge of Kaliakoir Police Station at the relevant time and he only filled in the FIR form. PW 4 A Majid Sarker is a former Chairman of Fulbari Union Parishad within PS Kaliakoir. PW 5 Md Iman Ali is a member of the Ward of the said union parishad in which Abdus Sattar was residing with his second wife before he was murdered. PW 6 Alef Kha and PW 7 Palu Mia are co-villagers of the victim Abdus Sattar. PW 8 Md Julhash is a 10(ten) year old minor son of victim Abdus Sat tar and he was 8 (eight) years old and sleeping with his mother and father in the same but when the occurrence took place. PW 9 Momrej Ali is a full brother of victim Abdus Sattar. PWs 10 and 11 Jamsher Ali and Tamser Ali are co-villagers of victim Abdus Sattar. PW 11 was merely tendered for cross-examination by the prosecution. 

 10. PW 12 Yad Ali is another co-villager of the victim Abdus Sattar and he was a village policeman at the relevant time. PW 13 Sukur Ali is a nephew of deceased Abdus Sattar and was living in the same village where the deceased was residing with his second wife. PW 15 Md Nurul Islam is a Magistrate who recorded the confessional statements of the accused appellants Jamila Khatun and Md Ali Hossain. 

 11. We find on careful scrutiny of the evidence that except PW 8 Md Julhash and his mother accused appellant Jamila Khatun there is no eye-witness to the occurrence. Since Jamila Khatun is an accused in this case PW 8 Julhash was examined as a solitary eye-witness to the occurrence. PWs 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 12 and 13 have only stated that on hearing the news of death of victim Abdus Sattar they all came to the place of occurrence and found Abdus Sattar dead with various bleeding injuries on various parts of his body including head, forehead and chest. They did not know who were responsible for causing the aforesaid fatal injuries. 

 12. It is, therefore, important to advert to and carefully consider the evidence of PW 8 Md. Julhash. This witness was aged about 8 years at the time of occurrence. He was there on the night of occurrence sleeping with his mother accused appellant Jamila Khatun and father victim Abdus Sattar. He stated that he was roused from his sleep by the scream of his mother Jamila Khatun and found accused appellant Habi who gave him a kick to shut him up. It is also stated by this witness that convict accused Jaban tied the hands and legs of his mother accused appellant Jamila Khatun while accused appellant Abdul held legs of his father Abdus Sattar and accused appellant Ali Hossain struck a knife blow on the neck of his father while accused-appellant Habi kept his torch focusing on the face of his father. When his father breathed his last accused appellants left the place of occurrence heading west. Thereafter, this witness went to the house of his cousin brother PW 13 Sukur Ali and narrated the occurrence to him. Thereafter he along with his cousin brother Sukur came to the place of occurrence house. This witness stated in cross-examination that he untied his mother Jamila Khatun. He also stated during cross-examination that he did not state to anyone before what he stated today before the Court except one Alam. This Alam, however, was not examined in this case. This witness further stated in his cross-examination that his father was murdered at the instance of his mother Jamila Khatun and he recognized the accused appellants by the torchlights used by them. 

 13. In view of the statements made by PW 8 before the Court, it is also important to consider the evidence of PW 13 Sukur Ali. Because PW 8 stated that immediately after the occurrence he went to his cousin brother PW 13 Sukur Ali and narrated the occurrence to him PW 13 in his evidence stated that he was informed about the occurrence by PW 8 Julhas and his mother Jamila Khatun immediately after the occurrence, but PW 8 did not tell him about his recognition of the accused appellants in the first place; but later on he (PW 8) disclosed that the accused appellants murdered his father. This witness (PW 13) also stated during cross-examination that PW 8 told him that he recognized the accused appellants with kupi lamp whereas he stated before the Court that he recognized the accused appellants with the torchlight used by them. It is also important to note at this point that PW 9 Momrej Ali, uncle of the informant, stated that nobody including PW 8 informed him that accused appellants committed the murder of his brother Abdus Sattar. 

 14. If we now consider the evidence of investigating officer PW 14 SI Md Sultan Ahmed, we find inconsistencies and contradictions in the evidence of PW 8 Julhas. Because this witness investigating officer during cross-examination stated that PW 8 Julhash stated to him that accused appellant Abdul held the hands of his father Abdus Sattar but he deposed before the Court that Abdul held the legs of victim Abdus Sattar. There is yet another contradiction found in the evidence of PW 8 Julhash, in that the investigating officer PW 14 stated in cross-examination that PW 8 Julhash did not tell him that accused appellant Jaban tied the hands and legs of his mother Jamila. If we consider the confessional statement of accused appellant Jamila, it is found that PW 8 Julhas was roused by the cry of his mother Jamila after accused appellant Ali Hossain cut the throat of Abdus Sattar by inflicting a knife blow. If this confessional statement of Jamila is correct then PW 8 was not supposed to see who among the accused appellants tied his mother, held the hands and legs of his father and who did the fatal knife blows on the threat of his father Abdus Sattar. 

 21. In this background of the case, the prosecution is now solely dependent on the solitary testimony of the child witness in this case, namely, PW 8 Julhash. PW 8 Julhash, as already stated above, is an eye-witness by virtue of his being present on the fateful night of occurrence in the place of occurrence but sleeping with his mother convict-accused Jamila Khatun and his deceased father Abdus Sattar before he was murdered. We have already examined and discussed various aspects of the evidence of this witness. Now the only important question is as to whether his evidence would be safe to rely on for basing the conviction of the accused appellants in this case. 

 24. In the case of Fazlul Huq Sikder vs State reported in 1 BLC 173 it is held by a Division Bench of this Division that the legal position was that before examining a child of tender age as a witness a Court should satisfy itself that the child was sufficiently intellectually developed to comprehend what he has seen and to give an intelligent account of it to the Court. If the Court was of opinion that by reason of tender age and defective or immature understanding the child could not have perceived the particular incident to prove which he was produced as a witness, the Court should not only refrain from administering the oath to him, but should also decline to examine him as a witness. But if the child, though of tender age, was found . to be intelligent to understand the question put to him and to give rational answers to those questions then this capacity to give evidence was on the same footing as that of any other adult. But in such a case it would be desirable for the Court before examining the child as a witness, to test his intellectual capacity by putting a few simple and ordinary questions to him and to record a brief proceeding so that the higher court may feel satisfied as to the capacity of the child to give evidence. 

 27. In the present case it is already noticed that the child PW 8 Julhash, although claimed to be an eye-witness to the occurrence, did not give out the factum of his recognition of the convict accused to anyone including his cousin brother PW 13 Sukur Ali at the first instance. PW 13 says that PW 8 told him the names of the accused appellants at a later stage. In the absence of the case diary (CD) on record, as it was not forwarded to this Court by the trial Court, although it ought to have been sent in the present case, we are unable to ascertain the date as to when the investigating officer recorded his statement. It should therefore be construed that the statement of the said child witness was not recorded immediately after the occurrence and, as such, there was possibility of coaching by his cousins and other relations in whose care and custody he was left after his mother Jamila was away in jail. Moreover, the trial Court did not make any endeavor to test this child witness as to his intelligence and capacity to understand questions and provide rational answers thereto by recording a short proceeding by putting some ordinary and simple questions. The said considerations were necessary to be kept in mind by the trial Court as PW 8 was only 8 years of age when he allegedly saw the occurrence. The trial Court in this case ought to have satisfied the above requirements because of such tender age of PW 8.
